concept: Chat-template and tool-declaration determinism as a cache-hit prerequisite
summary: Ollama stores tool properties and tool-call arguments in insertion-ordered maps (`ToolPropertiesMap`, `ToolCallFunctionArguments`). A renderer that loops with `.All()` therefore emits keys in the order the client's JSON had them.

facts.text: Ollama stores tool properties and tool-call arguments in insertion-ordered maps (`ToolPropertiesMap`, `ToolCallFunctionArguments`). A renderer that loops with `.All()` therefore emits keys in the order the client's JSON had them.
The Qwen3.5 renderer writes the tool block first, inside the leading system turn, and serialises each tool with `marshalWithSpaces`.
`marshalWithSpaces` runs `json.Marshal` and then inserts a space after every `:` and `,` that lies outside a string, to mimic Python `json.dumps` spacing.
The Qwen3.5 renderer renders an assistant `<think>` block only for assistant turns after the last real user query, unless the Qwen3.8 variant flag `alwaysRenderAssistantThinkBlock` is set.

The Qwen3-Coder renderer takes the first system message and drops later ones, and adds the default system text "You are Qwen, a helpful AI assistant that can interact with a computer to solve tasks." when tools exist but no system message does.

The Qwen3-Coder renderer emits extra schema keys (anything except `type` and `description` on a property, and anything except `type` and `properties` on the parameters object) through `renderAdditionalKeys`. That helper marshals the object, unmarshals it into a `map[string]any`, and ranges over the map.

Ollama moved newer models from Go `TEMPLATE` strings to registered renderer and parser pairs; the qwen3-coder renderer carries a TODO to match Python `json.dumps` spacing, and the later Qwen3.5 renderer added `marshalWithSpaces` to do so.
llama.cpp issue 26974 (2026-08-12) showed template render time growing quadratically with tool count; PR 27034 merged 2026-08-14 with byte-identical prompts.

Go does not define an iteration order for `range` over a map. In `renderAdditionalKeys`, a property that carries two or more extra keys (for example `enum` and `default`) can therefore render those keys in a different order on different requests of the same logical tool set, which breaks the cached prefix. This is inferred from the code and the Go language rule; no issue reporting it was found.
The Qwen3.5 renderer has no such map loop for tool schemas, so the hazard is specific to the qwen3-coder renderer path.

Because the tool block precedes the system text and all messages, adding, removing or reordering one tool, or an MCP server reconnecting with its tools in a new order, changes bytes at the start of the prompt and forces a full re-prefill.

Insertion-ordered storage makes determinism depend on the client: a client that re-serialises `parameters.properties` with sorted or hash-ordered keys changes the rendered bytes even though the schema is logically equal.

Template render time is paid on every request, including full cache hits. At 20 tools of 20 properties the bundled Command-R tool-use template took 0.43 s on llama.cpp before the fix, and 9.2 s at 50 tools of 50 properties.

None found. The two engines choose different layers for determinism: Ollama fixes key order in Go structures, llama.cpp relies on the Jinja template and `common_json` insertion order (see llama-cpp-jinja-capability-probes-chat-template.md).
Whether `renderAdditionalKeys` ordering has produced an observable cache miss on a real qwen3-coder deployment; no measurement exists.
Whether Ollama's prefix reuse compares tokens or text, which decides how much one reordered key costs.
Ollama `ToolPropertiesMap` and `ToolCallFunctionArguments` keep insertion order through an ordered map and expose it through `All()`.
Ollama `marshalWithSpaces` inserts a space after `:` and `,` outside string values after `json.Marshal`.
The Ollama Qwen3.5 renderer renders each tool with `marshalWithSpaces` inside the first system turn, before the system content.
The Ollama Qwen3.5 renderer renders assistant think blocks only for turns after the last user query unless the Qwen3.8 variant is used.
The Ollama Qwen3-Coder renderer ranges over a Go `map[string]any` when it emits extra tool-schema keys.
The Ollama Qwen3-Coder renderer keeps only the first system message and injects a default system message when tools exist without one.
llama.cpp issue 26974 measured chat-template render time of 0.43 s for 20 tools by 20 properties and 9.3 s for 50 by 50 on the Command-R tool-use template.
llama.cpp PR 27034 (merged 2026-08-14) fixed two quadratic terms in `gather_string_parts` and kept prompts byte-identical.
In Ollama's qwen3-coder renderer, two requests with the same tools can render extra schema keys in different orders.
A change in tool order or tool set alters the first system turn and invalidates the whole prefix cache on Qwen renderers.
